title: Starts building my own game
author: Formal-Discussion941
selftext:
That post i wrote for the purposes to share and get feedback, maybe get any suggestions about fast generating animations/sprites and other graphics for that   
About my project (generated with ai )

We're building a 2D open-world RPG with procedural generation. Here's the core tech:

# Three-Layer Generation

**Layer 1: Real Maps**

* Grab data from OpenStreetMap (actual cities, roads)
* Convert to game coordinates using turf.js
* Result: authentic geography, not random noise

**Layer 2: Biomes**

* Simplex Noise creates elevation + moisture maps
* These determine biome type (forest, desert, urban, etc.)
* 40+ biomes, each with its own ruleset

**Layer 3: Details**

* Cellular Automata for lakes/rivers
* Watabou algorithm for city layouts
* Place trees, rocks, buildings based on JSON density rules

# The Secret: Determinism

Every chunk is generated from a **seed-based RNG**. Same seed = same world forever. No need to store chunks, just regenerate them.

# ECS Architecture

We use **bitecs** — components are stored in typed arrays, not objects. Fast and scalable.

https://reddit.com/link/1rkhsmk/video/8zmf8xod60ng1/player

    Entity + Components (data) + Systems (behavior)

NPCs are just entities with components like `Position`, `NpcRole`, `Memory`, `Traits`.

# Data-Driven Everything

* **NPCs:** JSON files with traits, schedules, reactions
* **Dialogue:** Ink files (the language from Heaven's Vault)
* **Items, Quests:** Same — all in JSON
* **No gameplay logic in code**

comments.author: fued
comments.body: This is a mix of incredibly generic stuff and buzzwords, it reads more like a marketing post lol

replies.author: Formal-Discussion941
replies.body: Actually, no, I just asked the agent in the IDE to tell me briefly about my game (I warned that the description was generated by AI). If I describe what I have put into the generation so far, these are various noises for different needs and algorithms such as Hydraulic Erosion, Tensor Fields, WFC, they are used differently, some for objects, some for cities and landscapes, etc., in general, I like the Azgaar’s Fantasy Map Generator project, everything is generated quite lively there, I want to have some of my generations similar to those, by the way, the project does not pursue any commercial goals, I’m just making a game for myself (and maybe someday I will share it with others). Initially, I intended to train the game on map data and some of the code remained from this (maybe that’s why he mentioned some unrelated technologies), by the way, I’m from a Russian-speaking country and in general I explain everything through a translator because he now translates better than me

replies.author: Formal-Discussion941
replies.body: I'm currently searching for a way to properly generate assets/sprites and other graphical content. I've settled on comfyUI + a local model and improved pixel art, but maybe someone here could suggest some tried and tested best practices for this (because I feel like I'm building a bicycle). I have everything stored in JSON structures, so it will be relatively easy for me to automatically generate content.

replies.author: Formal-Discussion941
replies.body: It's funny, but I've only been developing it for 3-4 days and I've never had much experience in game development, but I worked as a full-stack developer.

comments.author: fluchw
comments.body: So the terrain cannot be destroyed?

replies.author: Formal-Discussion941
replies.body: For now, at this stage of development, the terrain will not be destructible (if you mean the landscape itself). I am currently working on the generation itself and the basic foundation of the game, thinking through the general rules of interaction and so on, but in the future we could think about this, I think it will not be too difficult to implement.

replies.author: Formal-Discussion941
replies.body: In general, as a goal of the game, I like to explore something and find some beautiful locations, so I work on generation. In Minecraft, for example, I liked to walk around the world, find some villages or biomes, explore them more than dig in a mine, create mechanisms, or fight monsters.
